disclaimer: These are independently authored exploratory learning questions, not statements of the lab's active research agenda or claims of novel findings.

questions.title: What determines whether a massive binary survives a supernova?
questions.summary: Trace compact-remnant formation, natal kicks, and orbital changes to understand which systems stay bound.
questions.activity: Sketch two contrasting post-supernova outcomes and identify which physical assumptions drive the difference.

questions.title: Which stellar histories can produce merging black-hole binaries?
questions.summary: Compare mass transfer, common-envelope evolution, and alternative formation channels without assuming one universal pathway.
questions.activity: Compare two modeled formation channels and record the assumptions that change their predicted outcomes.

questions.title: How might metallicity and stellar winds influence black-hole populations?
questions.summary: Follow how initial composition can affect mass loss, massive-star evolution, and the masses of compact remnants.
questions.activity: Make a qualitative prediction for how changing wind strength might affect a model population, then identify what you would need to simulate.

questions.title: How do simulated binaries become predictions for cosmic merger rates?
questions.summary: Connect population-synthesis outputs, statistical weights, delay times, and cosmic star formation.
questions.activity: Outline the input quantities and transformations needed to estimate a merger-rate history from a synthetic population.

questions.title: How does detector selection change what we infer about black-hole populations?
questions.summary: Contrast the intrinsic distribution of sources with the subset detected, then examine how population inference accounts for that difference.
questions.activity: Draw a hypothetical intrinsic and detected population, and explain where selection enters the inference.

questions.title: What would it take to reproduce a population-synthesis result?
questions.summary: Work backward from a reported plot to simulation outputs, parameter choices, code, and reproducibility checks.
questions.activity: Choose a public example, list required inputs, and define what would count as a successful reproduction.
